system_graph.reading: Everything the economy touches funnels through five hubs that do not exist yet (watch clock, Regard graph, thread runtime state, office/pretext/funds runtime state, actor/provenance on effects). The built reducer cases are leaves hanging off hubs that are not there.

findings.claim: The economy/levers graph has no hub nodes in code: WorldState has no watch clock, no funds/hooks/pretext state, no office or thread runtime state and no Regard graph, so every built reducer case is a leaf whose design-stated writers and readers are all unbuilt; the sole real consumer is a camera tilt.
findings.bites_when: Change 06 (utility AI/threads/offices) or 05b (clocks): each needs to add a hub field to WorldState AND rewrite every leaf that was shaped before the hub's contract was known.
findings.disconfirm: grep for every WorldState field consumer in src: pressureStocks, discoveryLayer, availableDelta have no reader outside reducer and snapshot copy; activeEmergencyId and orbital burn are read only by RenderFrameBuilder. No office/thread/funds field exists in WorldState or in stateSlices usage.
findings.recommendation: Adopt the system_graph table in this file as the roadmap's dependency spine, and add the hubs (watch clock, actor-tagged effects, thread runtime slice, player resource ledger) before any further leaf reducer cases. See S2B-04 and S2B-06.
findings.ignore_cost: Each later system lands as another leaf wired to a guessed hub, and the reducer is rewritten at 06.

findings.claim: The only economic coupling in the game (instrument -> stock -> discovery layer, with a 0.25 factor and fixed layers) is hardcoded inside the domain reducer, not data, so P1/P4 tunability and content skinning of the three instrument modes cannot work.

evidence.quote: The three abstract modes stay identical across all configured Epochs while their content skin evolves per rung

findings.bites_when: First time anyone wants Epoch 4 forged letters to be less traceable than Epoch 1 counterfeit coin, or wants to tune bullion's subsistence hit: the number lives in a switch in src/domain.
findings.disconfirm: Looked for an InstrumentEffectProfile / coupling table in EpochBlueprints.ts or content: none. The detection tech level that DESIGN_NOTES:18 says should scale discoverability has no field anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Make the reducer generic: the effect carries or looks up a data profile {stockDeltas: Record<stock, number>, discoveryFloor, scar?} registered per epoch pack; the three modes become default profile keys, not switch branches.
findings.ignore_cost: Tuning the economy means editing domain code, and Epoch skins cannot alter mechanics.

findings.claim: As built, the pressure/discovery loops have no balancing side and no dynamics: stocks change only when an effect is dispatched, discovery can only ratchet up, and forged fiat jumps straight to 'attributed', which the design says triggers rival strikes, so the first forged coin is a one-way trip.

evidence.quote: Triggered when `discoveryLayer >= 'attributed'`, when pulling ahead on a Butterfly Thread, or when your Ship Mind is `occluded`.
Flows continuously as the three macroeconomic gauges of any age

findings.bites_when: First playtest where an instrument is used twice, or a long idle: stocks sit forever (dead equilibrium) while discovery only climbs (runaway to fixed rival strike). Implied loops: R1 bullion->subsistence->unrest->emergency->pretext->more insertion is reinforcing and has no cap but clamp01; B1 stock decay, B2 discovery cooling/evidence fading, B3 absorptionCapacity (DESIGN:177) are the balancing loops and none has a writer or a field.
findings.disconfirm: Checked for any decay/relaxation reducer or per-watch drift handler: the only per-step code is advance_orbital_pass regen. The design does name the balancing pieces (Clock 4 drift, absorptionCapacity), so this is 'unbuilt', not 'undesigned' -- but nothing records which loop each is meant to close, nor the parameters.
findings.recommendation: Write the 4-6 loops as one table (reinforcing/balancing, stock, writer, tuning key) in DESIGN_NOTES and give each balancing loop a named data key (stockDecayPerWatch, discoveryCoolingWatches, per-layer evidence half-life) in the pacing profile. Make discovery a decaying evidence score with thresholds rather than a max() ordinal.
findings.ignore_cost: Either the economy never moves (dead) or it runs away after one bad move, and both look like bugs to a player who cannot see numbers (P4).

findings.claim: Time is currently three incompatible units: schema fields are *Ticks, behaviors are seconds, worldTick is an effect-batch serial that is also stamped onto legacy scars as if it were time, and the specified elapsedWatches clock does not exist in WorldState.

evidence.quote: Monotonic integer watches (`watchesPerDay`, `daysPerSeason`, `epochWatchBudget`) advanced when the player performs **Committed Time-Spend Actions**

findings.bites_when: 05b (clocks) is the declared rebase, but 06 and 08-class content will be authored against *Ticks names before then; any save made now stamps scars with an effect serial that means nothing after the rebase.
findings.disconfirm: Searched for elapsedWatches/Watch in src: no matches. Searched config/DESIGN for a decision record on tick vs watch: only the 4-clock section, which says it will rebase fields later. Pass: the 4-clock hierarchy itself is sound (see keep). CLOCK MODEL AS IT STANDS: Clock 1 elapsedSimulationSeconds (real, seconds; deliberation/dwell/cooldown/earshot) -- exists. worldTick -- exists, is an effect-apply counter, not time. Clock 2 elapsedWatches -- designed, absent; owns stipendPerTick, baseTransitTicks, fuseTicks, orbital *DurationTicks, burnCostPerTick, orbitalOffsetTicks (all still *Ticks in schema). Clock 3 storyteller -- designed, absent, consumes Clock 2. Clock 4 drift -- designed, absent, 'per watch / per season'. DECISION RECORD that unblocks schema work (five lines): (1) Sim-time unit for all macro durations is the integer Watch; days and seasons are pure derived functions of watches via the pacing profile, never stored. (2) Rename every macro *Ticks field to *Watches now (zero content uses them, so the rename is free). (3) Seconds belong only to Clock 1 and never cross into a blueprint macro field. (4) worldTick is renamed effectSeq, is telemetry-only, and legacy scars get stamped with watch. (5) Watches advance only through one effect, advance_watches{n, cause: enum}, so the storyteller, drift and telemetry hook one place. References: King of Dragon Pass is the nearest model (one decision per season, the season is the atom, events fire at turn boundaries); Pentiment bounds days with hard act structure and advances time only at location/commit transitions, which matches 'committed time-spend'; RimWorld's storyteller works because the whole sim is one tick unit and incidents are drawn on an interval, so a single unit with a derived calendar is the proven shape; Frostpunk shows the cost of a visible time unit (daily fixed pressure from temperature) and that a legible countdown (law gates, storm) is what makes pressure feel fair.
findings.recommendation: Write the five-line decision record into DESIGN_NOTES and openspec config before the next time-bearing schema, and rename the *Ticks fields while they have zero users.
findings.ignore_cost: The rename later touches schemas, tests, saves, pacing profiles and AI eval fixtures instead of seven unused fields.

findings.claim: Leverage Chain is named as the payoff for finding two pillars resting on one person, but the pillar schema cannot express 'bears on a thread' or 'rests on a node', the thread blueprint uses one opaque float, and the reducer can only delete a pillar, so the chain cannot be defined without a schema change.

evidence.quote: In any era, identifying that two pillars rest on the same person/institution lets a clever player topple both with one Leverage Chain.

findings.bites_when: Change 06 implements 'Inertia Pillars & Leverage Chains' in one change title with no definition to implement; DESIGN:16 says Ignorance/Debt harden into Doctrine/Constituency, but there is no way to add a pillar or change its kind.
findings.disconfirm: grep -i 'leverage chain' returns only DESIGN_NOTES:16 and openspec/config.yaml:91,134, all naming it. holderEntityId could be 'rests on', but then nothing says which thread the pillar bears on; the pillar is stored on an entity, whose relation to a thread is undefined.
findings.recommendation: PROPOSED DEFINITION: a pillar gets bearsOnThreadId and supportedBy: {entityId | institutionalLineageId}. Thread inertia becomes derived (sum of live pillar weights, with initialInertia dropped or used as a ceiling). A Leverage Chain is a derived query, not stored state: the set of live pillars on a thread that share a supportedBy node, plus the lever axes that move that node (Regard.respect/obligation/exposure, an Office pretext, a debt/hook). The player verb is weaken_support(node, axis, amount); it reduces every pillar on that node and emits a pillar_fracture event per pillar toppled. Chain strength = pillars toppled per verb; this is exactly the 'one action, two pillars' payoff. Add adjust_pillar_weight and add_pillar effects so hardening (Ignorance->Doctrine) is expressible; collapse stays as the zero-weight special case.
findings.ignore_cost: The headline puzzle mechanic of the thread system is built as a flat numeric slider.

findings.claim: Eight rules constrain engine architecture today and are unwritten: clock unit, actor/provenance on effects, thread structure, discovery referent and escalation, one-vs-many emergencies and fuse state, legal-action validation without throwing, player resource ledger, and what epoch-end export reads.
findings.bites_when: 05d-05f/06/07 start: each rule is a field or signature that more than one future change will depend on.
findings.disconfirm: Checked whether each is answered anywhere: epoch-end export reads only scars (SimulationCoordinator:728) and the design (DESIGN:15) says stocks carry forward but the export drops them; whether any effect carries an actor (none does); whether fuse state exists (fuseTicks has no state counterpart).
findings.recommendation: RULES SPINE (rule -> code it constrains): (1) Clock = Watch, see S2B-04 -> EpochBlueprints *Ticks, WorldState, SimulationCoordinator.advanceTick. (2) Every WorldEffect carries an actor and cause {player, npc, rival, system, epoch} so discovery can attribute and telemetry can log -> WorldEffectSchema, reducer signature, DiscoveryLayer. (3) A Thread is a runtime state machine {phase: omen..resolution, pillarIds, derived inertia, verbs available, resolution outcome}, one slice per thread, with single crisis_fuse enforced by the director, not a float -> TrajectoryThreadBlueprint, new ThreadRuntimeState. (4) Discovery is a per-observer or per-trail evidence score with thresholds, naming a referent (which faction, which instrument), not one global ordinal -> WorldState.discoveryLayer, maxDiscoveryLayer. (5) Emergencies are a list with a fuse countdown and an affected-scope, cardinality decided now (design implies trial + plague + blackout can overlap, only blackout is exclusive) -> activeEmergencyId, compound_emergency_vices (currently hits ALL entities). (6) Illegal player actions return a rejection result via a pure canApply predicate; reducers do not throw for gameplay conditions -> spend_orbital_delta. (7) A player resource ledger exists (funds, hooks as Regard.obligation, pretext charges, delta) since the Office stipend and fund spend have nowhere to land -> WorldState, OfficeBlueprint.stipendPerTick. (8) Epoch-end evaluation reads a declared set: both scar ledgers, thread resolutions, pressure stocks snapshot, discovery trail, Regard/lineage edges -> exportLegacyState, RecordedLegacyScar (no severity, weight or lineage field).
findings.ignore_cost: Each is a breaking schema change once 06 content and saves exist.

findings.claim: Of the three economic concepts, orbital Delta is the only real decision (borrow time, pay later), but it is completely uncoupled from illicit insertion and pretexts, while the three pressure stocks are bookkeeping gauges and discovery layers are an unlabelled global rank, so none yet gives the player something to feel or weigh.

evidence.quote: Player can spend **Delta (Orbital Indiscretion)** to **Slingshot** (arrive early, lengthening next occlusion) or **Burn** (linger at zenith, leaving a stationary-star omen in the sky).

findings.bites_when: Epoch 1 vertical slice: the player asks 'what does dropping bullion cost me, and why would I not do it every zenith?' and the answer in code is nothing.
findings.disconfirm: Looked for orbitalPass or availableDelta in the insert case: absent. Also considered that DESIGN:18 might intend only Slingshot/Burn as Delta uses; but then 'Orbital Insertion Modes' (DESIGN:14) are named for the orbit and never need it. VERDICTS. Pressure stocks: bookkeeping as designed (3 global scalars, no region, class or stock-flow). Player feels them only if they surface as diegetic price/ration/queue changes in rooms Vane, Mara and Orin inhabit; give each a signature tell (bread weight, nail price, gift inflation). The decision becomes interesting when stocks differ by district or class, so a drop hurts one group and relieves another. Discovery layers: interesting if framed as who knows what (the guild assays, the Synod attributes, the rival theorizes), each with a different consequence and a different cover-story that can contain it; as a global rank they are a hidden timer. Orbital Delta: the best candidate, and it should be the price of every insertion (cost scaled by intensity and gated by zenith) so Delta, discovery and stocks form one budget triangle.
findings.recommendation: Make insert_illicit_instrument spend Delta and require zenith (or a horizon discount), return a rejection otherwise, and give each stock a district/class split plus a named diegetic tell. Re-key discovery by observer.
findings.ignore_cost: The three systems stay independent dials that never trade off, so there is no decision and nothing to tune.

keep.claim: The 4-clock hierarchy (room seconds vs committed-watch macro time vs storyteller vs slow drift) is the right shape: it explains why a 50-100 hour campaign does not tick on the room clock, and copies the proven RimWorld/KoDP pattern of one macro unit with a storyteller drawing on it.

Scars to CivilizationLegacyState to applyLegacyToCharacterBlueprints is the only complete write, read, world-change arc in the economy, and the dual material/veil ledger prevents single-score optimization. Protect it as the template for every other system.

Pillars as concrete, named supports (not one float) is a good lever design: it turns resistance into a puzzle the player can read from NPC behaviour (P4). The schema just needs the relation fields in S2B-05.

evidence.quote: Resistance is composed of 3–5 concrete pillars

unconsidered_routes.title: Evidence-trail discovery instead of a ladder
unconsidered_routes.proposal: Replace the global discoveryLayer rank with a small list of Traces {kind (assay-fail, rumor, intercepted letter, sky omen), subjectId, observerFactionId, strength, watchCreated}. Layers noticed/assayed/attributed/theorized become derived thresholds per observer, and traces decay per watch unless reinforced. Rival strikes, trials and extracted_overt read the trace list, and the same list is what the notebook shows as partial knowledge and gaps (S1-R5).
unconsidered_routes.reference: Crusader Kings secrets (who knows which secret) and Hitman's witnessed/recorded-evidence model, where investigation reads traces; contrast Dishonored-style global chaos counters.
unconsidered_routes.replaces_or_changes: WorldState.discoveryLayer, set_discovery_layer, maxDiscoveryLayer; gives inference trails (S1-R2) a concrete data structure.

unconsidered_routes.title: Stock-flow economy with visible tells, not gauges
unconsidered_routes.proposal: Model the three pressures as per-district stocks with inflow/outflow per watch (Frostpunk resource flows, Dwarf Fortress price drift) and show them only through 3 diegetic tells per stock authored by content. Insertions are flows with a decaying half-life and a Delta price, so 'one drop' is a bump that relaxes and 'three drops' is a regime change.
unconsidered_routes.reference: Frostpunk resource/heat model; Victoria 3 supply-demand per market; Offworld Trading Company's visible price pressure.
unconsidered_routes.replaces_or_changes: PressureStocksState (3 clamp01 scalars) and the hardcoded 0.25 in the reducer; gives the balancing loops of S2B-03 a home.

unconsidered_routes.title: Storyteller as a card deck over the thread state machine
unconsidered_routes.proposal: Run Clock 3 as a seeded draw over authored beats gated by thread phase, tension envelope and recovery floor, with the F3 pacing lab previewing deck order. Each thread advances only on a drawn beat or a player verb, never by its own timer.
unconsidered_routes.reference: RimWorld storytellers (Cassandra/Phoebe tension curves), Left 4 Dead director, King of Dragon Pass seasonal event draws.
unconsidered_routes.replaces_or_changes: Gives 'point-release cadence' (DESIGN:106) an implementation shape and removes any per-thread timer fields from TrajectoryThreadBlueprint.
